fact.claim: Hut 8 reported its third-quarter 2026 results on November 4, 2026. Before the market opened, the stock fell 20.62%, from a previous close of $88.90 to $70.57. That means $1,000 of shares would have been worth about $794 right then, a drop of about $206. This was the premarket price only, not the closing price, and the move came after revenue of $71.1 million missed estimates. Almost all of that revenue, $68.4 million, came from the Compute segment, which covers ASIC bitcoin mining machines, AI Cloud and Traditional Cloud together. The release does not report mining and AI separately. Power brought in $1.3 million and Digital Infrastructure (colocation) brought in $1.4 million.
